Chapter 10: The Practice of Gratitude and Presence.
In a world that just never seems to slow down, it’s so easy to miss those little moments of beauty—the quiet joys that slip into our days almost unnoticed.
Gratitude isn’t just a feeling. It’s something you practice. It’s a way of looking at the world that can turn even the most ordinary days into something truly meaningful.
Here’s a simple ritual you might find helpful: at the end of each day, take a moment to notice three things that brought you joy or comfort. Maybe it’s a warm cup of coffee, a kind word from a stranger, or just the sound of rain tapping on your window. Some days, finding those moments is easy. Other days, it takes a little more effort—but honestly, it’s the act of looking that makes all the difference.
Over time, you’ll notice your mind starts to catch the good stuff, even when life feels tough.
Let me share a quick story. There was a man who struggled with anxiety. He decided to keep a gratitude journal. At first, his entries were tiny—almost forced. But as the weeks went by, something shifted. His worries didn’t just vanish overnight, but they lost some of their hold. Instead of always focusing on what was missing, his mind started to see what was already there. Life felt a little lighter, a little more hopeful.
Presence is a practice, too. It’s about choosing to be here—right now—instead of getting lost in regret about the past or worry about the future. Most of us spend so much time replaying old conversations in our heads or planning what’s next. But when we bring our attention back to the present—to our breath, our body, the world around us—there’s a sense of peace. A kind of enoughness.
Gratitude and presence really do go together. When you practice both, you build a foundation for real joy, for resilience, and for a life that feels rich and full—no matter what’s happening around you.
